LESSON: CREATING

Grade: PP2
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: CREATING
Topic 4.1: Creating

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Creating. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What is your favourite shape?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use digital device to create ICT devices randomly 4. Which digital device do you shapes and forms creativity • Guide learners to create like using

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CREATING
Subject: PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Creating helps you succeed in PSYCHOMOTOR AND CREATIVE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: CREATING
Study Creating like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Use digital device to create ICT devices randomly 4. Which digital device do you shapes and forms creativity • Guide learners to create like using

What this means
In this part you learn to use digital device to create ICT devices randomly 4. Which digital device do you shapes and forms creativity • Guide learners to create like using. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use digital device to create ICT devices randomly 4. Which digital device do you shapes and forms creativity • Guide learners to create like using.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Creating” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use digital device to create ICT devices randomly 4. Which digital device do you shapes and forms creativity • Guide learners to create like using. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Creating is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Creating” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: use digital device to create ICT devices randomly 4. Which digital device do you shapes and forms creativity • Guide learners to create like using)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Creating to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use digital device to create ICT devices randomly 4. Which digital device do you shapes and forms creativity • Guide learners to create like using.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Creating from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Creating: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Creating?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What is your favourite shape?
2. Which form do you enjoy USING ICT 4 lessons devices shapes and forms using drawing most?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Creating means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use digital device to create ICT devices randomly 4. Which digital device do you shapes and forms creativity • Guide learners to create like using.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
